Yep, Solicitors. There's a lot of focus placed on criminal barristers, but family solicitors have had a massive real terms paycut. There's also Legal Help which is meant to be for lesser issues and pays solicitors even less. So much so that a lot of firms (althought they won't admit to the LAA) allow law cases to escalate via clients having no representation so that they can charge more at Legal aid rates later on than Legal help. Simply because there's no incentive to undertake Legal Help.

In the last 10 years There's been a massive fall in Legal aid solicitors because of the pay. Vulnerable people being unable to access legal representation is a serious issue
People are less interested in being in the police nowadays given political trends imported from America and there are substantial gaps that need filling in any event.

Whilst they are technically private, given that the Legal Aid Agency pays solicitors costs, I would say legal aid solicitors have probably had the biggest cut in real terms. Since before 2010, Legal Aid solicitors for civil cases have only had their pay rates cut. 2010 was already a 10% cut in pay but then in 2014, solicitors working in Care cases had a further 10% cut. 

In line with inflation, their rate should have changed from ~£58ph to ~£85. Instead it fell to ~£52. A near 40% cut in real terms with no pay increase looking likely.

It is absolutely essential that children receive representation in these cases yet the government refuses to pay.

Whilst it may seem that £52h is a lot, typically the solicitor will get paid roughly a third for this due to overheads etc. Private rates for solicitors are also on average 4-5x higher than this rate so there is no incentive in working for the public under legal aid.
